findings.description: The KMS key protecting the audit bucket has no enable_key_rotation = true, so AWS will never automatically rotate the backing key material. A long-lived, never-rotated data key increases the blast radius and exposure window if the key material is ever compromised.

No aws_kms_key_policy (or policy argument) is defined for this key, so it falls back to the permissive default key policy that grants the entire AWS account root principal full kms:* control. Any principal in the account that can assume root-equivalent permissions can administer, disable, or re-key the audit encryption key; an explicit least-privilege key policy should restrict administration and usage to the audit principals.
